newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Japan PM hopes Peru talks with rebels resume soon.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM hopes Peru talks with rebels resume soon.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Monday he hoped direct talks to free 74 hostages held by Marxist rebels at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima would resume as soon as possible.

Hashimoto told a news conference near the end of a five-nation tour of Southeast Asia that planned direct talks between the Peruvian government and the rebels on Sunday had been called off because the rebels demanded the release of 400 of their imprisoned comrades.
"The situation remains extremely tough and difficult allowing no pre-judgement," he told the news conference. "We hope direct negotiations will be resumed as soon as posssible."

Armed rebels of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement stormed a diplomatic reception at the Japanese ambassador's residence on December 17, taking more than 500 hostages and demanding the release of jailed comrades.
Most of the captives have since been released in batches but none has been freed since New Year's Day. Government negotiators say they will not give in to rebel demands.
Hashimoto said his government had complete faith in Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori and supported his government's refusal to "yield to terrorism".
"We very much hope tenacious efforts will be made to free the hostages in a peaceful resolution," he said. "We have complete faith in the Peruvian government."
The 74 captives still held include dozens of Peruvian officials and Japanese businessmen as well as Fujimori's younger brother, Pedro, and the Japanese and Bolivian ambassadors.
